stories.title: Creation
stories.sourceCaption: God named him Adam and put him in a garden he had planted in Eden. Adam worked and looked after the garden. – Slide 13
stories.license: CC BY-SA; see source page for version

stories.title: Noah and the Ark
stories.sourceCaption: God put a rainbow in the sky. God then told Noah, ‘This rainbow is the sign of my promise never to flood the whole earth again.’ – Slide 24
stories.license: CC BY-SA; see source page for version

stories.title: Abraham
stories.sourceCaption: When the sun had set a smoking firepot with a blazing torch appeared and passed between the carcasses Abram had laid on the ground. God promised Abram to give his descendants the land from the Wadi of Egypt to the river Euphrates. – Slide 10
stories.license: CC BY-SA; see source page for version

stories.title: Joseph
stories.sourceCaption: So with severe famine everywhere, Joseph opened up the storehouses and distributed grain to the Egyptians. – Slide 8
stories.license: CC BY-SA; see source page for version

stories.title: Moses
stories.sourceCaption: So Moses decided to take a closer look. Suddenly God called to him from inside the burning bush, ‘Moses.’ ‘Here I am Lord,’ Moses replied. – Slide 3
stories.license: CC BY-SA; see source page for version

stories.title: Joshua and Jericho
stories.sourceCaption: When the trumpets blasted and the army shouted, the walls of the city collapsed. – Slide 11
stories.license: CC BY-SA; see source page for version

stories.title: Ruth
stories.sourceCaption: So Boaz married Ruth and the Lord blessed them with a son. Women told Naomi, ‘Praise the Lord. He has looked after you in your old age. Ruth loves you and is better to you than seven sons.’ Ruth and Boaz’s son was called Obed. Obed was the father of Jesse whose youngest son David became King of Israel. A descendant of David was Mary the mother of Jesus. – Slide 11
stories.license: CC BY-SA; see source page for version

stories.title: Samuel
stories.sourceCaption: ‘Here I am. Did you call me?’ Eli realised it was the Lord who was calling Samuel. So he said, ‘Go and lie down again, and if someone calls again, say, “Speak, Lord, your servant is listening.”’ – Slide 12
stories.license: CC BY-SA; see source page for version

stories.title: David and Goliath
stories.sourceCaption: As Goliath started walking toward David again, David ran quickly toward the Philistine. He reached into his bag and took out a stone, which he slung at Goliath. It hit him on the forehead, breaking his skull, and Goliath fell face downward on the ground. – Slide 16
stories.license: CC BY-SA; see source page for version

stories.title: Solomon
stories.sourceCaption: ‘Give the living baby to the first woman. Do not kill him; she is his mother.’ When the people of Israel heard the verdict they held the king in awe, because they saw that he had wisdom from God to administer justice. – Slide 13
stories.license: CC BY-SA; see source page for version

stories.title: Elijah
stories.sourceCaption: Elijah continued, ‘I am the only one of the Lord’s prophets left, but Baal has 450 prophets. Get two bulls for us. Let Baal’s prophets choose one, cut it into pieces and put it on an altar of wood. But they must not set fire to it. I will prepare the other bull and put it on an altar with wood. But I will not set fire to it. Then, you call on the name of your god, and I will call on the name of the Lord. The god who answers by fire—he is God.’ The people agreed to the contest. – Slide 12
stories.license: CC BY-SA; see source page for version

stories.title: Jonah
stories.sourceCaption: Immediately the wind dropped and the sea became calm. Jonah sunk under the water. But God has not finished with His disobedient prophet. He has prepared a great fish to swallow Jonah and keep him alive. – Slide 9
stories.license: CC BY-SA; see source page for version

stories.title: Daniel and the Lions
stories.sourceCaption: Daniel answered, ‘May your Majesty live forever! God sent His angel to shut the mouths of the lions so that they would not hurt me. He did this because I was innocent.’ The king was overjoyed and gave orders for Daniel to be pulled out of the pit. – Slide 12
stories.license: CC BY-SA; see source page for version

stories.title: Esther
stories.sourceCaption: Haman went to his friends and Zeresh his wife and boasted to them about his great wealth, his many sons and the ways the King had honoured him. ‘I have been invited to a banquet by the King and queen tomorrow. But I cannot be happy while Mordecai the Jew is sitting at the King’s gate.’ – Slide 13
stories.license: CC BY-SA; see source page for version

stories.title: The Birth of Jesus
stories.sourceCaption: That night Mary gave birth to her first born son. She wrapped him in cloths and placed him in a manger. – Slide 15
stories.license: CC BY-SA; see source page for version

stories.title: Jesus Calms the Storm
stories.sourceCaption: The weather was calm when they set off and Jesus was very tired. He lay down to sleep on a cushion in the back of the boat. – Slide 4
stories.license: CC BY-SA; see source page for version

stories.title: The Good Samaritan
stories.sourceCaption: ‘Then a Samaritan who was traveling that way arrived on the scene. When he saw him, his heart was filled with pity. He went over to him, poured oil and wine on his wounds and bandaged them – Slide 9
stories.license: CC BY-SA; see source page for version

stories.title: The Prodigal Son
stories.sourceCaption: ‘So he returned home to his father. While he was still a long way off, his father saw him coming. Filled with love and compassion, he ran to his son, embraced him, and kissed him. – Slide 12
stories.license: CC BY-SA; see source page for version

stories.title: The Crucifixion
stories.sourceCaption: ­ Those who passed by hurled insults at Jesus, shaking their heads and saying, ‘You said you would destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days. Come down from the cross and save yourself.’ – Slide 5
stories.license: CC BY-SA; see source page for version

stories.title: The Resurrection
stories.sourceCaption: John arrived first and stared into the empty tomb. He saw strips of linen lying there but did not go in. Simon Peter caught up and went straight into the tomb. – Slide 10
stories.license: CC BY-SA; see source page for version
